title: Hotel Cash Flow Forecast with Claude (Excel Add-in)
goal: Build and validate an automated monthly hotel cash flow forecast that consolidates operating and property-level cash movements and calculates projected owner funding requirements.
context: I currently work in hotel asset management, where part of my role involves reviewing property-level financial performance, cash balances, operating results, and owner funding requirements. A recurring challenge is consolidating information from different financial sources into a monthly cash flow that clearly shows the expected cash position and whether additional owner funding is required. I chose this goal because it combines financial analysis, classification decisions, Excel modeling, validation, and management reporting. It is complex enough to require several dependent steps and professional judgment, but it can be substantially advanced within a one-hour working session using anonymized or non-sensitive data.

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: I reach the cash flow ending balance

Step-1.step_name: Review, clean, and map the source information
Step-1.step_action: Review the available opening cash balances, budget/P&L information, payment schedules, and any supporting cash flow files. Identify which data points are required for the model, standardize the monthly periods, and create a mapping between each source line and the appropriate cash flow category. Use Claude to challenge the mapping logic and identify any potentially missing cash flow items.

nodes.label: Assess and orient to source data
nodes.detail: The participant opens 'Minesota - Sources.xlsx' from Windows Explorer and tours the workbook, reviewing the P&L tab (Jan–Jun actuals), Movements tab (~300 raw bank transactions across 5 accounts in USD and MXN), Bancos tab (monthly bank balances with implied FX rate 17.5), and Categories tab (keyword-to-category mapping table).

nodes.label: Commission AI to categorize bank movements
nodes.detail: The participant selects the Movements tab, opens the Claude for Excel sidebar (Opus 4.8), and prompts Claude to add a Category column between Description and Inflow using the keyword-to-category mapping defined in the Categories tab.

nodes.label: Generate initial category classification for all movements
nodes.detail: Claude (Opus 4.8) adds a Category column using an IFERROR/INDEX/MATCH lookup formula that assigns Spanish-language labels (Cobranza, Pago a Proveedores, Nómina, Gastos de Operación, Gastos de Propiedad, Conciliación) to all ~300 movement rows across all 5 bank accounts.

nodes.label: Review the initial category classification for all movements
Spot-check initial categorizations
nodes.detail: The participant reviews Claude's first-pass categorization row by row, cross-checking domain knowledge for hotel and winery transactions. They determine the Spanish labels should be switched to English.

nodes.label: Identify translation need
Translate category labels to English via mapping table update
nodes.detail: Claude adds an English column to the Categories tab mapping table and updates the lookup formula to return English labels: Cobranza→Collections, Pago a Proveedores→Supplier Payments, Nómina→Payroll, Gastos de Operación→Operating Expenses, Gastos de Propiedad→Property Expenses, Conciliación→Reconciliation. Confirms all 300 rows classified with zero uncategorized.

nodes.label: Validate categorizations account-by-account
nodes.detail: The participant scrolls through all 300 movement rows across the 5 bank accounts, verifying that English category labels correctly reflect transaction descriptions. They check for hotel-specific entries (OTA commissions, hotel payroll) and winery-specific entries (harvest supplies, vineyard maintenance), and inspect the Categories tab keyword map for completeness.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source: a2 Requests for a English Column to categories 
Target: a7
Reasoning: Accepts column

nodes.label: Build cross-check pivot table to reconcile monthly balance totals
nodes.detail: The participant inserts a PivotTable on Sheet2 (Sum of Running Balance by Account × Month) to reconcile that monthly ending balances in the Movements tab match the Bancos tab summary. They later reconfigure the pivot to Account × Day for a daily running-balance audit.

nodes.label: Filter and verify per-account June movements
nodes.detail: The participant filters the Movements tab by specific bank account and date range (June 2026) to manually validate each account's net movements and running balance totals against the Bancos tab, confirming data completeness and accuracy before proceeding to the cash flow build.

Step-2.step_name: Design the monthly cash flow structure and classification logic
Step-2.step_action: Define the cash flow statement structure, including beginning cash, operating inflows/outflows, property-related expenses, CapEx, debt or financing items, taxes, owner contributions, and ending cash. Establish the logic for how each mapped source item will flow into the forecast.

nodes.label: Create Cash Flow tab and establish structural skeleton
nodes.detail: The participant adds a new 'Cash Flow' tab, sets the Currency assumption cell to MXN with a data-validation list (MXN/USD), adds an FX Rate reference cell, labels section 1 'Initial Balance / Cash Flow', and formats the period column header for June 2026.

nodes.label: Anchor initial cash balance from source data
nodes.detail: The participant adds the Initial Cash row for June 2026, linking via cross-sheet reference to the Bancos tab to pull the total bank balance as of end-May (MXN 2,919,393) as the opening balance for the cash flow model.

Step-3.step_name: Build the automated Excel calculations and roll-forward
Step-3.step_action: Build the monthly formulas and linkages that pull the mapped inputs into the cash flow, calculate net monthly cash movement, and roll ending cash into the following month's beginning balance. Use formulas that can be copied across periods and minimize manual hardcoding. Add basic checks so that broken links, missing periods, or inconsistent balances are visible.

nodes.label: Prompt Claude to import June P&L summary into Cash Flow tab
nodes.detail: The participant selects the target range on the Cash Flow tab and instructs Claude to pull a summarized version of the June P&L from the '2026' tab using live cross-sheet formula links in green font (per the participant's finance-report convention).

nodes.label: Generate condensed P&L section with live cross-sheet links
nodes.detail: Claude (Opus 4.8) generates a P&L summary block with ='2026'!Hxx formula references in green, pulling Total Revenue (6,169,748), Profit Hotel & Winery, Non-Operating Dept. Expenses (2,554,511), G.O.P. (114,385), Fixed Costs, EBITDA, Other Expenses, and Net Income (−2,164,260) for June.

nodes.label: Evaluate P&L output and identify missing revenue and expense detail
nodes.detail: The participant opens a second Excel window to compare the Cash Flow P&L section against the source 2026 tab side-by-side, finding Total Revenue needs individual line breakdowns (Habitación, AyB, Otros Ingresos Hotel, Vinicola, Otros Ingresos Vinicola) and Hotel/Winery Expenses must appear separately for Profit subtotals to compute correctly.

user_response.label: modify
user_response.reasoning:
Source: Requests for summarized version of P L Summary 
Target: c2
Reasoning:  modify as user makes changes on cells

nodes.label: Prompt Claude to populate per-account bank net movements for June
nodes.detail: The participant creates Section 3 'Property Expenses / Other Expenses / Other Movements' on the Cash Flow tab, selects the Bank Account Movements range, and instructs Claude to populate each of the 5 bank accounts' net movement for June with expenses negative and inflows positive.

nodes.label: Detect cross-currency conflict and solicit user decision
nodes.detail: Claude identifies that the Movements Net column stores USD-account amounts in raw USD while the Cash Flow tab is denominated in MXN. Rather than assume a treatment, Claude presents an interactive Ask User Question widget with options: '1. All in MXN', '2. Native currency + label', 'Something else'.

nodes.label: Decide to standardize all amounts to MXN
nodes.detail: The participant selects option '1. All in MXN', directing Claude to convert USD-account net movements to MXN using the FX rate referenced from the Bancos tab (17.5 MXN/USD), keeping the Cash Flow tab in a single consistent currency.

nodes.label: Build SUMIFS formulas with USD-to-MXN FX conversion
nodes.detail: Claude generates SUMIFS formulas filtered to June 1–30 per bank account, multiplying USD-account totals by the FX rate (17.5) when the account identifier contains 'USD'. Links all 5 accounts: Bank A USD 2566 (877,623 MXN), Bank A MXN 1462 (−401,470), Bank A MXN 5376 (90,010), Bank C USD 0091 (160 MXN), Bank C MXN 2368 (418,887). Total Net Movements: 985,209 MXN.

nodes.label: Manually verify per-account net movements against filtered source data
nodes.detail: The participant switches to the Movements tab, applies Date and Account filters for each of the 5 accounts in June, and hand-checks inflow/outflow totals (e.g., USD account 2566 inflow $93,852.98) against Claude's generated figures, confirming that USD-to-MXN conversions are correct.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source: c4 Prompt Claude to populate her account bank net movements 
Target: c5: Builds conversion formulas 
Reasoning: Adopt, does not modify formula

nodes.label: Calculate and validate ending balance
nodes.detail: The participant adds Section 4 'Ending Balance' with the End of Period Balance formula (Initial Cash + Net Income + Total Net Movements = 1,740,343 MXN), then cross-checks by manually dividing a USD balance by 17.5 to confirm the FX conversion is consistent with the Bancos tab.

nodes.label: Request dual-currency FX toggle formula for entire Cash Flow tab
nodes.detail: The participant configures the Currency cell as a data-validation dropdown (MXN/USD), then prompts Claude to wrap specific P&L and movements cells (C8, C13–C17, C28, C31, C34, C40–C44) with an FX-toggle formula: if Currency = MXN leave as-is, if USD divide the value by the FX rate in C3 (17.5).

nodes.label: Apply currency-toggle IF(TRIM) wrapper and self-diagnose coverage gap
nodes.detail: Claude wraps the specified cells with =IF(TRIM($C$2)="MXN", <original_formula>, <original_formula>/$C$3), using TRIM to handle trailing spaces in the Currency cell, explains the formula logic in the sidebar, and confirms cross-sheet links remain intact. Claude then proactively flags that C20 and C23 were outside the user-specified cell list and that its own USD toggle test produced a broken 0.63 ratio, proposing to apply the same IF(TRIM) wrapper to C20 and C23 to resolve the coverage gap.

nodes.label: Accept diagnosis and apply corrected formula to missing cells
nodes.detail: The participant accepts Claude's diagnosis and manually enters the IF(TRIM($C$2)="MXN",...) wrapper formula for C20 (Hotel Expenses) and C23 (Winery Expenses) in the formula bar, then reverts Currency to MXN to check that the MXN figures are restored correctly.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source: Asks Claude to add fx effects on selected cells
Target: c11
Reasoning: Accepts, makes some modifications by updating the formula, but is suggested by Claude.

nodes.label: Test and validate the MXN/USD currency toggle across all P&L lines
nodes.detail: The participant switches Currency from MXN to USD to test the toggle, discovering a broken ratio (~0.63) in Net Income and End of Period Balance traced to Hotel Expenses (C20) and Winery Expenses (C23) cells omitted from Claude's formula update, causing mixed-currency arithmetic. After Claude applies the fix, the participant reverts to MXN and retests, then performs a final MXN↔USD toggle confirming that all P&L lines, bank account movements, and the End of Period Balance convert consistently in both currencies. They paste-as-values a few cells to resolve an AutoSave conflict and confirm the final Ending Balance as the session's primary deliverable.

Step 1.step_name: Review, clean, and map the source information
Step 1.step_action: Review the available opening cash balances, budget/P&L information, payment schedules, and any supporting cash flow files. Identify which data points are required for the model, standardize the monthly periods, and create a mapping between each source line and the appropriate cash flow category. Use Claude to challenge the mapping logic and identify any potentially missing cash flow items.
Step 1.input: Anonymized Excel files containing opening bank balances, monthly P&L/budget data, and property-level payment schedules; existing cash flow template if available.
Step 1.output: Cleaned source data and a documented mapping of source items into operating, property-level, financing, and other cash flow categories..
Step 1.tools: Microsoft Excel (Microsoft 365); Claude; Cap IQ for FX Rates
rubrics: All required source files and monthly periods are identified and organized
Each material source line is mapped to one clear cash flow category
No obvious duplicate or missing categories remain after review
The mapping distinguishes operating cash flow from property-level/non-operating and financing items
The mapping is understandable enough that another finance professional could follow it

ratings.output_quality_reason: The output was clear and useful and covered the material cash flow categories. Claude helped me think through classifications and identify items I might otherwise have misscategorized:

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Why Claude accelerated the review and mapping process and helped challenge my classification logic, while I kept final judgment over the financial treatment.?

Step 2.step_name: Design the monthly cash flow structure and classification logic
Step 2.step_action: Define the cash flow statement structure, including beginning cash, operating inflows/outflows, property-related expenses, CapEx, debt or financing items, taxes, owner contributions, and ending cash. Establish the logic for how each mapped source item will flow into the forecast.
Step 2.input: Mapping created in Step 1, existing cash flow template, budget/P&L categories, and known property-level obligations..
Step 2.output: Final monthly cash flow layout and classification rules ready to be implemented in Excel
Step 2.tools: Paid version: Microsoft Excel (Microsoft 365); Claude Max.
rubrics: The cash flow structure rolls logically from beginning cash to ending cash
Operating, property-level, CapEx, financing, and owner funding items are clearly separated
Each mapped source item has a defined destination in the model
The structure supports a monthly forecast and can be extended to future periods
The layout is concise and useful for management review

ratings.output_quality_reason: The final structure was logical, easy to follow, and management-oriented. Claude was especially useful for checking whether operating, property-level, CapEx, financing, and owner funding items were separated consistently.:

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The agent helped organize the cash flow structure and pressure-test the classifications, which reduced the time needed to design the model.?

Step 3.step_name: Build the automated Excel calculations and roll-forward
Step 3.step_action: Build the monthly formulas and linkages that pull the mapped inputs into the cash flow, calculate net monthly cash movement, and roll ending cash into the following month's beginning balance. Use formulas that can be copied across periods and minimize manual hardcoding. Add basic checks so that broken links, missing periods, or inconsistent balances are visible.
Step 3.input: Final structure from Step 2 and cleaned/mapped source data from Step 1.
Step 3.output: Working automated monthly cash flow model in Excel with linked inputs, formulas, balance roll-forward, and control checks..
Step 3.tools: Paid version: Microsoft Excel (Microsoft 365). Paid version: Claude Max only if formula troubleshooting or logic validation is required.
rubrics: Ending cash for each month correctly rolls into the next month's beginning cash
Formulas are consistent across the forecast periods and avoid unnecessary hardcodes
The model captures all mapped cash inflows and outflows
Control checks identify missing or inconsistent data
The model updates correctly when an input assumption changes

ratings.output_quality_reason: The model worked and the roll-forward logic was completed. Claude made one incorrect suggestion during formula or logic troubleshooting, so I had to verify and correct it manually, but it still helped me diagnose the issue much faster and reduced trial and error.:

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Even though one suggestion was wrong, the agent was very helpful in troubleshooting, explaining alternatives, and getting to the correct formula after I redirected it.?

Step 4.input: Automated cash flow model from Step 3, minimum cash requirement, payment timing assumptions, and selected scenario assumptions..
Step 4.output: Monthly owner funding requirement, scenario comparison, and identification of the months with the highest liquidity pressure..
Step 4.tools: Paid version: Microsoft Excel (Microsoft 365); Claude Max.
rubrics: The funding formula is directly linked to projected cash and the minimum cash threshold
Owner contributions are triggered only when required by the model logic
At least one meaningful alternative scenario is tested
The model clearly identifies the timing and amount of peak funding needs
Scenario results are financially reasonable and traceable to changed assumptions

ratings.output_quality_reason: The funding logic and scenario analysis were useful and financially consistent. Claude helped identify edge cases and interpret when projected cash would create an owner funding requirement.:

goal_achievement.Why or why not: Claude helped test the logic and made it easier to identify the periods with the greatest liquidity pressure and explain the scenario results.?

Step 5.input: Completed cash flow model, source data, control checks, and scenario results from Steps 1-4..
Step 5.output: Validated Excel cash flow forecast plus a concise management summary of liquidity, key cash drivers, and projected owner funding requirements.
Step 5.tools: Paid version: Microsoft Excel (Microsoft 365); Claude Max.
rubrics: Key cash flow totals reconcile to the underlying source data or differences are clearly explained
No material formula errors, broken links, or unexplained balance movements remain
The final summary identifies the most important cash flow drivers and funding periods
Conclusions are supported by the model and do not overstate what the data shows
The final output is clear, concise, and suitable for review by a hotel asset manager or owner

ratings.output_quality_reason: The final model was validated and the summary clearly communicated the main cash drivers and funding requirements. Claude improved the clarity of the conclusions and helped challenge whether the commentary was fully supported by the model.:

goal_achievement.Why or why not: The agent helped with the final review and made the management summary clearer and faster to prepare without replacing my own financial judgment.?
